overview.what_it_is: This lesson teaches how to find a triangle's area. Its area is half its related rectangle.

format_facts.label: Main skill
format_facts.value: Find a triangle's area from its base and height.

format_facts.label: Related rectangle
format_facts.value: The rectangle has the same base and height.

scoring_factors.name: Correct base
scoring_factors.what_it_measures: You choose the side used as the base.

scoring_factors.name: Correct height
scoring_factors.what_it_measures: You use the straight height to the base.

scoring_factors.name: Correct working
scoring_factors.what_it_measures: You multiply, then take one half.

scoring_factors.name: Correct units
scoring_factors.what_it_measures: You give the answer in square units.

critical_rules: The height must meet the base at a square corner.
Do not use a sloping side as the height.
Multiply the base and height, then halve the result.
A triangle has half its related rectangle's area.
Write square units after every final area answer.

learning_goals: You will identify a triangle's base and height.
You will use the triangle area formula correctly.
You will find half a related rectangle's area.
You will solve simple area word problems.
You will check units and spot common errors.

core_method.name: Choose → Check → Multiply → Halve → Label
core_method.summary: Choose the base and straight height. Multiply them. Halve the product. Add square units.

steps.detail: Pick a base. Find its straight height.
Make sure they meet at a square corner.
Write the answer using square units.

techniques.name: Use the related rectangle
techniques.purpose: Shows why the triangle area is halved.
how_to: Draw a rectangle with the same base and height.
Place the triangle inside the rectangle.
Find the rectangle using base times height.
Take half to find the triangle's area.
techniques.example: A $6$ by $5$ rectangle has area $6 \times 5 = 30$ square units. Its triangle has $30 \div 2 = 15$ square units.
techniques.why_it_matters: The picture explains the formula, not just the rule.
techniques.common_error: Using the whole rectangle's area for one triangle.

techniques.name: Find the straight height
techniques.purpose: Uses the correct distance from base to top.
how_to: Choose one side as the base.
Look for a line meeting it squarely.
Use that straight line as the height.
Ignore a sloping side unless it meets squarely.
techniques.example: For base $10$ cm and straight height $7$ cm, use $\frac{1}{2} \times 10 \times 7 = 35\text{ cm}^2$.
techniques.why_it_matters: A sloping side gives the wrong related rectangle.
techniques.common_error: Using the longest side as the height.

techniques.name: Halve an even factor first
techniques.purpose: Keeps the numbers smaller and easier.
how_to: Look at the base and height.
Choose an even number to halve.
techniques.common_error: Halving both the base and the height.

techniques.name: Check with the rectangle
techniques.purpose: Tests whether the answer is reasonable.
how_to: Compare the triangle answer with it.
The triangle answer must be exactly half.
Check the square unit at the end.
techniques.example: The rectangle is $8 \times 5 = 40\text{ cm}^2$. The triangle should be $40 \div 2 = 20\text{ cm}^2$.
techniques.why_it_matters: This catches forgotten halves and wrong products.
techniques.common_error: Accepting an answer larger than the rectangle.

worked_examples.title: Triangle inside a related rectangle
worked_examples.input: A triangle fills half a $6$ by $5$ rectangle. Find its area.
worked_examples.decoding: The rectangle and triangle share the same base and height.
worked_examples.plan: Find the rectangle's area. Then divide by $2$.
worked_examples.model_answer: First find the related rectangle's area. $6 \times 5 = 30$ square units. The triangle is half the rectangle. $30 \div 2 = 15$ square units. The triangle's area is $15$ square units.

annotations.comment: This finds the full rectangle's area.
One triangle fills half the rectangle.
Area always uses square units.
It clearly states the triangle's area.

worked_examples.title: Right-angled triangle
worked_examples.input: Find the area of a triangle with base $6$ cm and height $8$ cm.
worked_examples.decoding: The base and height meet at a square corner.
worked_examples.plan: Use half times base times height.
worked_examples.model_answer: Use the triangle area formula. $\text{Area} = \frac{1}{2} \times \text{base} \times \text{height}$. Put in the known lengths. $\text{Area} = \frac{1}{2} \times 6 \times 8$. Halve $6$ first. $\text{Area} = 3 \times 8 = 24\text{ cm}^2$. The triangle's area is $24\text{ cm}^2$.

annotations.comment: The values replace the base and height.
Halving $6$ first makes the work easy.
The answer uses square centimetres.
It answers the question in words.

worked_examples.title: Sloping triangle with an outside height
worked_examples.input: A sloping triangle has base $10$ cm and straight height $7$ cm. Find its area.
worked_examples.decoding: Use the straight height, even when it lies outside.
worked_examples.plan: Multiply base and straight height. Then take half.
worked_examples.model_answer: The sloping side is not the height. Use the straight height of $7$ cm. $\text{Area} = \frac{1}{2} \times 10 \times 7$. Halve $10$ first. $\text{Area} = 5 \times 7 = 35\text{ cm}^2$. The triangle's area is $35\text{ cm}^2$.

annotations.comment: It meets the base at a square corner.
The correct base and height are used.
Halving first keeps the numbers small.
This is half the related rectangle's area.

worked_examples.title: Triangular garden sign
worked_examples.input: A triangular sign has base $12$ cm and height $9$ cm. Find its area.
worked_examples.decoding: Bar model in words: one rectangle is split into two equal triangle areas.
worked_examples.plan: Find half the area of a $12$ by $9$ rectangle.
worked_examples.model_answer: The related rectangle has base $12$ cm and height $9$ cm. Its area is $12 \times 9 = 108\text{ cm}^2$. The sign has half the rectangle's area. $108 \div 2 = 54\text{ cm}^2$. The triangular sign's area is $54\text{ cm}^2$.

annotations.comment: The rectangle shows two equal area parts.
This finds the related rectangle's area.
The sign has half the rectangle's area.
The final answer includes square units.

worked_examples.title: Correcting a forgotten half
worked_examples.input: Mia says a triangle with base $8$ cm and height $5$ cm has area $40\text{ cm}^2$. Is she correct?
worked_examples.decoding: Mia found the rectangle's area, not the triangle's area.
worked_examples.plan: Check her product. Then take half.
worked_examples.model_answer: Mia worked out $8 \times 5 = 40\text{ cm}^2$. That is the related rectangle's area. A triangle has half that area. $40 \div 2 = 20\text{ cm}^2$. Mia is not correct. The triangle's area is $20\text{ cm}^2$.

annotations.comment: This product is correct for the rectangle.
The missing step is taking one half.
The answer checks the claim directly.
This is exactly half of the rectangle.

items.when_to_use: The side chosen for the bottom of the work.
The straight distance from base to the top.
A square corner between base and height.
A rectangle with the same base and height.
The space covered inside a flat shape.
The answer after multiplying two numbers.
A short maths rule used many times.
Combine the base and height sizes.
Find half of the rectangle's area.
Name the unit used for any area.
Test that the triangle is half the rectangle.
State the side chosen as the base.
Show which height you will use.

common_mistakes.why_it_hurts: You give the full rectangle's area.

common_mistakes.mistake: Using a sloping side as the height.
common_mistakes.why_it_hurts: It does not make the right rectangle.
common_mistakes.fix: Use the line meeting the base squarely.

common_mistakes.why_it_hurts: This makes the answer four times too small.
common_mistakes.fix: Halve only one factor, or halve the product.

common_mistakes.mistake: Writing centimetres instead of square centimetres.
Choosing two lengths that do not match.
common_mistakes.why_it_hurts: The base and height must form one pair.
common_mistakes.fix: Check they meet at a square corner.

time_budget.focus: See why a triangle has half the area.
Correct errors and explain each step.

drills.name: Rectangle then half
drills.instructions: Find four rectangle areas. Divide each answer by $2$.

drills.name: Spot the height
drills.instructions: Look at six triangles. Mark each straight height.

drills.name: Halve first
drills.instructions: Solve six questions by halving an even factor first.

drills.name: Unit check
drills.instructions: Fix five answers with missing or wrong square units.

drills.name: Explain the error
drills.instructions: Read four wrong solutions. Say what went wrong.

practice_plan.routine: Practise for twenty minutes. Draw, work, check, then explain aloud.

mastery_checklist: I can choose a triangle's base.
I can find the matching straight height.
I can write the triangle area formula.
I can multiply the base and height.
I can take half of the product.
I can use a related rectangle.
I can write square units correctly.
I can correct a forgotten-half error.
strategy_notes: Draw a small square corner beside the height.
Halve an even factor before multiplying.
Estimate using the related rectangle first.
Your triangle answer must be half the rectangle.
Circle the square unit before finishing.
Explain why each chosen height matches its base.
